record.original_question: For the QR algorithm applied to random matrices, can one control, as n tends to infinity, the bulk eigenvalue-ratio statistics |lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j| and |lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j| near the eigenvalue lambda_j closest to zero, together with the associated normalized eigenvectors, so as to prove the analogue of the Toda-algorithm universality theorem for QR?

evidence.quote: It is very much an open problem to control, as n -> infinity, the statistics of |lambda_{j+1}/lambda_j|, |lambda_{j-1}/lambda_j| for lambda_j ~ 0 deep in the bulk of the spectrum, together with their associated normalized eigenvectors, as in (8), (9). The QR algorithm is the "go to" algorithm for eigenvalue computation, and the proof of the analog of Theorem 1 for the QR algorithm is an open problem of great interest.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be an $n\times n$ real symmetric (or complex Hermitian) random matrix drawn from a Wigner-type ensemble (with i.i.d. centered entries of unit variance above the diagonal, suitably normalized so that the empirical spectral distribution converges to the semicircle law on $[-2,2]$). The shifted QR eigenvalue algorithm produces a sequence of orthogonally (unitarily) similar tridiagonal matrices $H = H_0, H_1, H_2, \dots$ defined by $H_k - s_k I = Q_k R_k$ (QR factorization) and $H_{k+1} = R_k Q_k + s_k I$, where $\{s_k\}$ is a chosen shift strategy (e.g., the Wilkinson shift). Order the eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ of $H$ and let $j = j(n)$ be an index for which $\lambda_j$ is closest to $0$ (i.e., deep in the bulk).

Prove the following analogue of the Toda-algorithm universality theorem for the QR algorithm: as $n\to\infty$, the joint distribution of the bulk ratios
$$\Big(\big|\lambda_{j+1}/\lambda_j\big|,\ \big|\lambda_{j-1}/\lambda_j\big|\Big)$$
together with appropriate functionals of the associated normalized eigenvectors of $\lambda_{j-1},\lambda_j,\lambda_{j+1}$, when properly centered and scaled, converges to a limiting distribution that does not depend on the particular Wigner ensemble (i.e., is universal across the choice of entry distribution), and use this to deduce universality of the halting-time / deflation statistics of the shifted QR algorithm at indices in the bulk of the spectrum.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is described in the literature as a well-known open problem. Universality for the Toda algorithm has been proved (Deift–Trogdon and related works), and analogous empirical universality has been observed numerically for QR, but a rigorous proof of bulk eigenvalue-ratio and eigenvector universality controlling the QR halting time remains unestablished as of the most recent publicly available work. No paper claiming a complete proof was found.

status_evidence.title: How long does it take to compute the eigenvalues of a random symmetric matrix?
status_evidence.snippet: Universality observed empirically for the shifted QR deflation times across ensembles; theoretical explanation not fully understood.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical, not proved: rigorous QR universality remains open.

status_evidence.title: Universality for the Toda algorithm to compute the eigenvalues of a random matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Toda-algorithm universality theorem established; analog for QR posed as open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The QR analog of the Toda universality theorem is stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Universality for Eigenvalue Algorithms on Sample Covariance Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Extends universality results to certain eigenvalue algorithms but does not establish full QR bulk-ratio universality.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on related algorithms; QR bulk universality not resolved.
